headline: Midterm Fallout and Hormuz Fires Frame Thursday's Open as Oil Whipsaws
body_html:
Traders approach Thursday's open still digesting the midterm elections, where Democratic gains have investors abroad betting on a softer line on trade and the Iran conflict. Indian benchmarks sat near three-month highs as oil slipped, though other reports showed crude firming again as investors weighed the danger of the Iran war widening.

Wednesday's session was constructive beneath the surface. Of the 525 stocks we track, 343 rose and 180 fell. Homebuilders led, up an average of 6.7%, followed by consumer names at 4.58%, healthcare at 4.29% and software at 2.6%. Energy shed 4.15% and semiconductors gave up 4.06%, the two weakest groups on the board.

For the open, watch whether oil holds its footing after Iran's Revolutionary Guard reported fires aboard two tankers and a tugboat in the Strait of Hormuz. Also watch whether the homebuilder rally extends, and how markets position ahead of a widely expected Bank of England rate hike, its first in three years. Pre-market moves are thin, so treat early prices with caution.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Set the Pace
briefs.body: Homebuilders were Wednesday's strongest group, up an average of 6.7%. Separately, TV commentary has focused on what Home Depot needs to keep alive a monthlong run of roughly 25%. Housing-linked names will be a key test of whether the bid carries into Thursday.

briefs.headline: Oil Pulls Both Ways
briefs.body: Energy stocks fell an average of 4.15% Wednesday as crude retreated on hopes the election result could lead the U.S. out of the Iran war. Later reports showed oil climbing again on escalation worries. Direction at the open may hinge on which narrative wins out.

briefs.headline: Fires Reported in Hormuz
briefs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Details remain thin. South Korea, meanwhile, plans to move its anti-piracy unit closer to the waterway, a sign of how closely shippers are watching the area.

briefs.headline: Bank of England Poised to Tighten
briefs.body: The Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates for the first time in three years. A move would mark a turn in the central bank's stance and could shape currency and bond trading in early European hours, with spillover to U.S. sentiment.

briefs.headline: Identity, Medical Supply Names Surge
briefs.body: Clear Secure jumped 23.7% and Medline gained 18.36% in Wednesday's session. UFP Technologies rose 17.66% and Trex climbed 14.3%. Healthcare and building-related names featured prominently among the day's top gainers, a pattern worth tracking at the open.

briefs.headline: Construction and Materials Names Hit Hard
briefs.body: Everus Construction dropped 29.29% and Sterling Infrastructure fell 21.46%. Innospec lost 18.72%, Forgent Power Solutions 17.32% and AAON 15.68%. The heavy losses in construction, power and HVAC stood out against a market where most stocks advanced.
